All three requested tests PASS on Expo web (mobile viewport 390x844) against public URL https://bot-burst-fix.preview.emergentagent.com. TEST 2 (full-chain back regression) — profile → /circle/{me} → /user/D → /circle/D → /user/Y → 4 back presses correctly walk one step per press: back1→/circle/D, back2→/user/D, back3→/circle/{me}, back4→/profile. critical_code_review_comments: Fix in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx is minimal and correct: a single useEffect keyed on usePathname() that calls navStack.clear() whenever pathname ∈ TAB_ROOTS (/, /top, /messages, /notifications, /profile). Runs at the Tabs layout level so it fires regardless of which detail screen is mounted underneath, catching every tab-root landing (initial navigation, tab-bar tap, and router.replace() back to root).

TAB_ROOTS set is authoritative — matches the five visible Tabs.Screen entries (index/top/messages/notifications/profile). If a future top-level tab is added, the constant must be updated too; consider deriving it from the Tabs.Screen config to avoid drift.

Clearing on EVERY tab-root landing (including initial mount) is safe because navStack is only populated by detail-screen useSmartBack push()es; tab roots never push themselves. So there is nothing legitimate to preserve at tab-root time.

rca_of_issue: PRE-FIX BUG (as described in review_request): navStack is a module-level singleton. Entries pushed by useSmartBack on detail-screen focus were NOT cleared when the user switched tabs via the tab bar (tab-bar tap only changes pathname, doesn't pop the manual stack). So sequence: profile→push('/circle/me')→tab-tap FAIDE (stack still contains ['/circle/me'])→open feud (stack: ['/circle/me','/feud/X'])→back from feud pops to '/circle/me' — wrong destination. FIX (verified in this iter): useEffect in TabsLayout listens to usePathname(); the moment pathname matches a top-level tab root, navStack.clear() runs. So after tab-tap FAIDE, pathname becomes '/', TAB_ROOTS.has('/')===true, stack is emptied; when feud is later opened, stack is ['/feud/X'] and back correctly falls through to the fallback ('/'). Same guard fires on MESSAGGI/NOTIFICHE/etc, so TEST 3 (multi-hop tab switching) also passes. Full-chain intra-detail back (TEST 2) is unaffected because no tab-root pathname is encountered mid-chain.
